children: urged the European Commission to ease restrictions on biofuel feedstocks ‌that do not put food supplies or forests at risk, Reuters reported Tuesday.

Biofuels, which are mostly produced from food and ​feed crops such as sugar and corn, are at the ​center of a disagreement over whether they help cut emissions and improve energy security or instead drive deforestation and higher food prices, so the European Commission currently limits ​the amount of biofuel feedstocks that can be grown in Europe.
believes such concerns do not apply to advanced biofuels made from intermediate ‌or ⁠cover crops such as canola grown between harvests or on degraded land.
"The maximum availability in Europe from these intermediate crops is up to 27M tons, but right now the certification rules disqualify a lot ​of the potential ​we have," ⁠Samuel Maubanc, Neste's
EMEA head of Public and Regulatory Affairs, said Tuesday at the Argus Biofuels Europe conference ​in London.
Crude oil prices have gained ~50% since the Iran war began in late February, sugar has surged ~40%, ​while corn has climbed 3%.
